name: Restfox
tagline: An HTTP client. Collections stay here. Requests leave when you send them.
description:
Build a collection of HTTP requests, press Send, and read the answer. Folders, query strings, headers, JSON or form bodies, Basic and Bearer auth, and {{environment}} variables — the same shape Restfox uses, kept on this device inside the app.

An unofficial port of Restfox by Flawid D'Souza (MIT). Restfox's own web-standalone is a Node server that proxies requests so the browser never has to; there is no Node here. Every Send goes through gifos.fetch, which is the only network path the sandbox has. Collections never leave. A request leaves this browser the moment you send it, https only, up to 8 MB back.

SAME LIMIT AS RESTFOX IN A BROWSER. Sites that do not send CORS headers will refuse the call — that is the browser talking, not this app being broken. Restfox's desktop app gets past that with its own proxy; this port does not. A checkbox can route through GifOS's CORS proxy, which only forwards to a curated public-host list, not arbitrary APIs. Cookies are never attached. There are no WebSockets, no plugins (the sandbox forbids eval), and no file workspaces.

The app asks to reach any site (network: *), so GifOS labels it ⚠ Unsafe and you confirm the hosts before it can talk. Untick one and that host is gone.
